about: Deep value with a margin of safety.

checks.msg: 1 holding(s) left out of the copy record because the ticker's price didn't match the price filed (often an old ticker now used by another company): IMOS.

summary: Concentrated: 21 holdings, but the top ten are 77% of the portfolio.
Trades a lot: about 70% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for 1.8 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are similarly priced, more profitable and much larger.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 1 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Born in 1957; Cornell and Harvard Business School. Worked at the Mutual Shares fund, then founded Baupost in 1982 with $27 million. Wrote Margin of Safety (1991).
profile.approach: Benjamin Graham-style value investing: buys unpopular assets well below their value, including distressed debt, and often holds a lot of cash.
known: Bought CIT Group bonds at 65 cents on the dollar in 2009; the fund finished 2009 up 27%.
Often holds 30–50% in cash, so the 13F shows only part of the picture.
profile.note: Much of Baupost's money is in bonds, private deals and cash, which the 13F does not show.

name: Seth Klarman
